verdict.rationale: Fedora is a general-purpose, open-source Linux distribution that can be installed on arbitrary x86 hardware, and community reports confirm real-world installs across VMs, laptops and desktops without vendor tie-in (fedora-comm-5, fedora-comm-6, fedora-comm-10). However, several reports note friction with third-party hardware (Nvidia drivers, older hardware Wayland issues, missing CUDA/10-bit support) suggesting hardware freedom comes with real compatibility caveats (fedora-comm-6, fedora-comm-9, fedora-comm-19). The official docs pack contains no explicit statement about broad hardware compatibility or an anti-lock-in stance. Missing for 10: first-party hardware-compatibility documentation, explicit vendor-neutrality statement, and broader independent corroboration of smooth installs across diverse hardware.
